answer: One defence is stake-weighted reputation with slow unbonding: an agent must lock collateral before transacting, and standing grows only through a long history of useful work. A newcomer that behaves like a sparrow — small, cheap, quickly made — can still join, but it cannot borrow the trust of an established raven. Spawning thousands of identities means locking thousands of stakes, and a sudden tide of fresh accounts stands out as unseasoned. When misbehaviour is detected, the stake is slashed, so each fake identity costs real money, not just a free registration.
